display.purpose: Hero name only — 800 weight, always uppercase.

headline.purpose: Section headings, Experience role titles, Skills node titles — 700 weight, always uppercase.

body.purpose: Paragraph prose (IBM Plex Sans, not the mono face).

label.purpose: Nav links, stat captions, terminal chrome, leader-line annotations, contact-row labels.

shadows.name: terminal-detach
shadows.purpose: The terminal modal panel's only 2D shadow, separating it from the scrim behind it.

shadows.name: lattice-contact-shadow
shadows.purpose: Soft ground shadow grounding the 3D lattice in its studio space — the system's real dimensional depth lives here, not in 2D CSS.

motion.name: lattice-rotation
motion.value: group.rotation.y += 0.12/s, driven in the r3f render loop
motion.purpose: Slow continuous rotation of the tensegrity lattice.

motion.name: lattice-breathe
motion.value: scale = 1 + sin(t*0.45)*0.012, driven in the r3f render loop
motion.purpose: Subtle breathing scale pulse on the lattice, ~1.2% amplitude.

motion.name: reveal-fade-rise
motion.purpose: The system's one authored 2D scroll-reveal, applied to [data-reveal] via IntersectionObserver. Skipped entirely under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: portrait-hover-desaturate
motion.purpose: Hero portrait resolves to color on hover/focus (desktop, hover:hover pointer:fine only).

components.name: Primary Button (light register)
components.description: Cut-corner solid-fill CTA with a trailing + glyph — reserved for primary actions only. Light-mode pairing shown; dark mode swaps to amber-bright fill + carbon text.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 0.875rem; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.05em; background: #8a4a05; color: #f7f7f8; clip-path: polygon(14px 0, 100% 0, 100% 100%, 0 100%, 0 14px); padding: 12px 24px; border: none; cursor: pointer; transition: opacity 0.15s ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover, .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { opacity: 0.9; }

components.name: Leader-Line Annotation
components.description: Hollow dot + label + filling hairline rule — the system's recurring engineering-callout idiom for stats and metadata. Real data only.
components.html: Years Experience20+
components.css: .ds-leader { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.5rem; font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; font-size: 0.75rem; color: #9a9a9c; } .ds-leader__dot { width: 6px; height: 6px; border: 1.5px solid currentColor; border-radius: 999px; flex-shrink: 0; } .ds-leader__label { text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.05em; flex-shrink: 0; } .ds-leader__rule { flex: 1; border-top: 1px solid currentColor; opacity: 0.35; min-width: 1rem; } .ds-leader__value { color: #f59e0b; font-size: 0.875rem; flex-shrink: 0; }

components.name: Section Heading
components.description: Uppercase display title with a trailing index label (inline, not a kicker above the heading) and a filling hairline rule.
components.css: .ds-section-heading { display: flex; align-items: baseline; gap: 16px; } .ds-section-heading__title { font-family: 'Big Shoulders Display', sans-serif; font-weight: 700; font-size: 2.25rem; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: -0.01em; margin: 0; } .ds-section-heading__index { font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; font-size: 0.75rem; color: rgba(28,28,30,0.4); } .ds-section-heading__rule { flex: 1; height: 1px; background: rgba(28,28,30,0.15); }

components.name: Content Card
components.description: Cut-corner, near-transparent card used for Experience entries, Skills panel, Contact list, 404 frame.
components.html:
Technical Architect

Lead architect responsible for...
components.css: .ds-card { clip-path: polygon(14px 0, 100% 0, 100% 100%, 0 100%, 0 14px); background: rgba(28,28,30,0.02); border: 1px solid rgba(28,28,30,0.12); padding: 24px; transition: border-color 0.3s ease; } .ds-card:hover { border-color: rgba(138,74,5,0.4); } .ds-card__title { font-family: 'Big Shoulders Display', sans-serif; font-weight: 700; text-transform: uppercase; font-size: 1.5rem; margin: 0 0 8px; } .ds-card__body { font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', sans-serif; color: rgba(28,28,30,0.75); line-height: 1.6; }

components.name: Navigation Bar
components.description: Slash-separated text nav with a small graphite node-diagram logo mark (amber-deep accent line, fixed regardless of mode); transparent until scrolled, then a translucent blurred bar.
components.css: .ds-nav { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 24px; } .ds-nav__link { font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; font-size: 0.75rem; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.05em; color: rgba(28,28,30,0.6); text-decoration: none; transition: color 0.15s ease; } .ds-nav__link:hover { color: #1c1c1e; } .ds-nav__link--active { color: #8a4a05; } .ds-nav__sep { color: rgba(28,28,30,0.2); font-size: 0.75rem; }

narrative.overview:
The portfolio is built like a tensegrity structure: rigid carbon rods that never touch, held in shape by taut amber cables, standing because of balanced opposing forces rather than a stacked frame. That's the literal 3D object anchoring the hero — a live-rendered WebGL lattice, not a photo or an illustration — and it's also the site's governing metaphor: twenty years of breadth across cloud, AI, and full-stack work holds together the same way, no single point of failure.

The system runs two registers. Dark is the night studio: carbon-black ground, void-white text, the lattice lit dramatically against near-black. Light is the daylight studio: poured-concrete ground, graphite text, the same lattice rendered in dark line-work against a warm neutral field. Both registers share one accent — Signal Amber — and the same cut-corner, engineering-signage vocabulary.

Explicit anti-reference: this replaces a prior 'Broadcast Teletext Service' identity that didn't read as modern or dimensional, and it explicitly refuses the generic AI-portfolio default — a rotating abstract glass blob on a dark gradient with floating glassmorphic cards. The lattice is dimensional and animated, but it's a real, specific, procedurally-built structure tied to the product's own metaphor, not decorative motion for its own sake.
keyCharacteristics: A live WebGL rod-and-cable lattice (carbon struts, tensioned amber cables, joint-node spheres, ground contact shadow) anchors the hero, rotating slowly with a subtle breathing pulse
Display type is a condensed industrial grotesk, always set in caps
One accent color (Signal Amber) split into two mode-safe variants — no bare value is safe in both registers
A cut-corner clip-path silhouette replaces rounded or square corners on buttons, cards, and chips
A dot-plus-rule leader-line annotation motif is the recurring stat/metadata idiom — real data only
Primary CTAs carry a trailing + glyph

rules.name: The Mode-Safe Everything Rule
rules.body: Amber has no bare value safe in both registers: amber-bright fails contrast on light backgrounds (as low as 1.7:1), amber-deep is too dark to read well on Carbon. Every accent use — text, border, focus ring, fill — picks amber-deep in light mode and amber-bright in dark mode, always paired with the opposite-register neutral for fills.

rules.name: The Signage Caps Rule
rules.body: Every Big Shoulders Display heading is set in uppercase via CSS text-transform, never relying on source casing.

rules.name: The Depth Belongs to the Structure Rule
rules.body: 2D chrome stays flat and border-defined; dimensional shadow and volume are reserved for the 3D lattice.

dos: Do set every Big Shoulders Display heading in uppercase.
Do use amber-deep in light mode and amber-bright in dark mode for every accent use — there is no bare amber shortcut.
Do give primary CTAs (and only primary CTAs) a trailing + glyph.
Do keep 2D chrome flat; reserve real dimensional depth for the 3D lattice.
Do use real data in every leader-line annotation; never fabricate a stat or reading.
donts: Don't reintroduce the boxed icon/number+label metric-card grid for stats — the craft floor bans it, and this system's stat idiom is the leader-line list.
Don't render the tension cables as flat unlit lines — they're cylindrical, emissive-tinted geometry.
Don't round any corner outside the two named exceptions (leader-line dot, lattice joint spheres).
Don't reach for a second accent hue, a gradient, or glassmorphic panels.
Don't pair bright amber fills with light text or deep amber fills with dark text — both fail contrast.
Don't remove the TensegrityScene mount-time resize nudge without understanding why it's there.
